Guides

Teething

Cold food and something firm to chew are enough. Amber necklaces and benzocaine gels are not.

Findings

Cold, not frozen solid, feels useful. A chilled cucumber stick, a cold spoon, or a soft-frozen fruit purée can help if the texture is already safe for that baby.
Skip benzocaine and lidocaine teething gels. Regulators warn against them in infants because they can affect the blood’s oxygen carrying and because they numb the gag.
Amber necklaces are a strangling and choking object. There is no good evidence that they reduce pain, and there are case reports of harm.

What is reasonable at the table

Teething can make gums sore and meals smaller for a few days. Keep offering the usual foods. Add something cold the baby can already manage: yogurt from the fridge, a peeled cucumber stick if they are chewing soft strips, or a fruit purée frozen until it is spoonable rather than rock hard. A hard lump of ice is its own choking and tooth injury.

Extra drool plus acidic fruit often reddens the chin. A plain barrier ointment and gentle washing do more than an allergy label. Wipe, do not scrub.

Gels and tablets

The US Food and Drug Administration advises against benzocaine teething products in children under two, because of methemoglobinaemia, and against viscous lidocaine for the same job. Numbing the mouth also makes choking more likely. In Europe, products aimed at infant teething have been restricted for the same reasons.

A clean finger rubbed on the gum is dull and effective. A dose of paracetamol or ibuprofen, in the infant formulation and at the dose your clinician has already approved, is the medicine conversation to have. It is not a food decision, and it is not for every grizzle.

Necklaces and other objects

Amber bead necklaces are marketed as a natural analgesic. The proposed mechanism is not credible at the dose a bead could release onto skin, and the object sits on the airway. The FDA has warned about choking and strangulation. Take them off for sleep and, better, do not use them.

Teething biscuits that are rock hard, or that are mostly sugar, fail both the choking test and the nutrition test. A piece of bread crust the baby already manages is a simpler chew.
